chapter_title: Chương 243: 0245【Quyết đấu giữa kẻ thấp kém và tư bản】

segments.title: Chương 243: 0245【Quyết đấu giữa kẻ thấp kém và tư bản】
segments.content:
Because of the CJ Electronics Expo, the hotels near the National Expo Center were all filled with personnel from Chinese and foreign game companies.

Chen Guiliang arrived at the hotel and met with Tao Chenggang first.

At this time last year, Tao Chenggang was still busy making his game, but now he was showcasing *Reign of Sovereignty* at the convention.

When the two met, besides talking about Tao Xue's college entrance exams, they naturally chatted about their respective games.

Chen Guiliang said that *Sanguosha's* monthly revenue had just broken the 10 million yuan mark last month.

Because the promotion and operation costs were relatively low, and they had their own payment system, the net profit was very substantial.

Adding in *Sanguosha's* overseas revenue share, profits from physical card sales, Youfutong's profits, and income from some smaller games, it all added up. Game Science's monthly net profit was estimated to be around 10 million yuan.

Even some players of *Reign of Sovereignty* were using Youfutong to top up their accounts.

There were two "ten million yuan" figures here. The former was just *Sanguosha's* online revenue, while the latter was the entire company's net profit!

A monthly net profit of over 10 million yuan was already incredibly impressive.

Tao Chenggang said, flushed with success, "*Reign of Sovereignty's* revenue this month will be at least 32 million yuan, and with good operations, it might approach 35 million. We're striving to reach the goal of 50 million in monthly revenue by the end of the year."

Chen Guiliang joked, "Your revenue figures actually didn't meet my initial expectations."

Hearing this, Tao Chenggang said with a pained expression, "Who knew a bunch of free-to-play games would pop up? Although *Yulgang* is almost dead, we have *Zhengtu*, *Eudemons Online*, and *Legend of Mir* snatching up the free-to-play market. This situation was completely unforeseeable."

"Hahaha." Chen Guiliang laughed without a care in the world.

Tao Chenggang sighed and said, "*Zhengtu's* promotion strategy is just impossible to compete with, and *Eudemons Online* is a damn marvel in its own right. Do you know how *Eudemons Online* does its promotions?"

"How do they do it?" Chen Guiliang played along.

Tao Chenggang said, "*Eudemons Online's* offline promotion team calls themselves the 'Cavalry Company' and even promotes some kind of 'Drawing Sword' spirit. In the internet cafes of second and third-tier cities, they go head-to-head with the *Zhengtu* team, shouting 'Cavalry Company, charge!' at the drop of a hat."

"If an internet cafe has already partnered with *Zhengtu*, the *Eudemons Online* team will just pay a premium to book out the entire place. They stand at the entrance of the cafe and shout that all the computers in the cafe have been paid for, and everyone can use them for free for the whole day. But they have to play *Eudemons Online*!"

"*Eudemons Online* will probably break into the top ten on 17173's monthly chart this month."

Chen Guiliang sighed inwardly. Shi Yuzhu wasn't the only one recklessly throwing money around.

Tao Chenggang faced immense competitive pressure making a free-to-play MMO.

*Sanguosha* was still more worry-free, with no competitors at all. Although its monthly revenue was far less than *Reign of Sovereignty's*, it could be a steady, long-term stream of easy money.

Chen Guiliang said, "I've bought the game adaptation rights for *My Own Swordsman*. The project has been approved, and we're building the development team. We plan to make it a free-to-play game as well."

"Holy crap. If you jump into this market, the competition is going to get even more intense," Tao Chenggang said.

One of the planners for *My Own Swordsman* had been confirmed to be Ning Caishen. He was responsible for fleshing out the game's entire worldview, properly rounding out the story that the TV series hadn't finished.

Hiring him was quite expensive, but he was worth the price, and he could also be used as a promotional gimmick.

For the lead planner position, Chen Guiliang wanted to promote Feng Ji.

Although this person was self-taught and his qualifications were so thin they were almost non-existent, according to feedback from the *Future Era* development team, Feng Ji learned incredibly fast.

In just a few short months, Feng Ji went from being an errand boy in the development team to one of the core planning staff.

He had played too many games, had a flexible mind, learned quickly, and also possessed a talent for management. It was only a matter of time before he stood out, provided he had the right platform to train on.

His only flaw was being too much of a perfectionist. Many members of the development team were already fed up with Feng Ji's nitpicking demands!

The next day, the CJ Electronics Expo began.

The GAPP and local leaders gave their speeches one after another, followed by presentations from the big shots at the main forum.

Which companies' big shots?

The unshakeable The9, NetEase, and Shanda, of course. These three were the most profitable game companies.

Don't be fooled by the apparent decline of *Legend of Mir* and *The World of Legend*, whose rankings on 17173's chart were dropping precipitously. The profitability of these two games was still not something emerging games could touch.

Furthermore, Shanda possessed the most comprehensive game top-up system in the country, with offline channels covering 70% of the nation's internet cafes.

A large number of small and medium-sized game companies used Shanda's payment system to process top-ups, and the commission they gave to Shanda each month was terrifying.

Chen Guiliang and Tao Chenggang were also invited to speak on stage, but their presentations were in a sub-forum.

When Tao Chenggang spoke, he mainly introduced his professional experience and how he made games to pursue his dream.

It couldn't be helped; he had to maintain his public image.

"After graduating from junior college, I got a job at a state-owned enterprise. For a young man from an 18th-tier small city, getting into a state-owned enterprise was the most perfect thing imaginable. But I wanted to see the outside world. I didn't want to be cooped up in a small place for my whole life, living a life where I could see the end from the beginning..."

"I quickly spent all the living expenses my parents gave me. To save money, I even slept on the streets in the Devil's City. It was still easy for junior college students to find jobs back then, but my standards were too high, and I had a terrible temper, so I always quit after a short time..."

"Later, when UTStarcom was expanding and hiring, I applied and became a PHS promoter. Then I was sent to third and fourth-tier cities to promote PHS, and I discovered that selling IC cards there was a blue ocean. So I quit and became an IC card agent. Calling it an agency was a stretch, I was really just a card scalper, and I earned my first bucket of gold, several hundred thousand yuan."

As he spoke about selling his internet cafe and car to make his game, and even being ready to sell his house, Tao Chenggang suddenly broke down in tears.

Superb acting!

Of course, it was mixed with genuine emotion. He had been truly worried back then, sometimes tossing and turning, unable to sleep all night.

Finally, Tao Chenggang spoke again about ensuring game quality and pursuing content innovation on that foundation. Blah, blah, blah.

The entire venue erupted in thunderous applause.

The founders of small game companies, in particular, felt a natural affinity for Tao Chenggang. They even saw him as an idol, dreaming that they too could one day successfully chase their dreams.

The story of a "grassroots" individual's counter-attack could resonate with kindred spirits anywhere.

In the past year, over a hundred new game companies had been established.

The founders of these small companies lacked everything but dreams. They came to the exhibition and game forum today for no other reason than to gain more support and resources.

They wanted to become the next Tao Chenggang!

This sub-forum was dedicated to discussions on free-to-play MMO games.

After Tao Chenggang finished, the next speaker was Shi Yuzhu.

The two were complete opposites.

Tao Chenggang kept talking about his lack of money to make games. And Shi Yuzhu?

"I've never been stingy when I do things. The initial R&D for *Zhengtu* cost 40 million, and most of that was spent on employee salaries. In the beginning, the R&D team only had 20 people, and as we worked, it eventually grew to 200..."

"For the initial 20-person team, I gave every single one of them company stock options and paid them the highest salaries in the entire industry. I also invested my own money, over ten million yuan, to build our own servers..."

"I've established branch offices in every province in the country, and we're going to push our offline promotions from second-tier cities all the way down to small county towns. My offline promotion team has already grown to over 2,000 people... I'm throwing 100 million US dollars in directly, with another 100 million US dollars as reserves!"

"Is there a secret to making games? It's actually very simple. The competition in this industry isn't as fierce as you might imagine. The rich are very rich. Ding Lei has 3 billion in cash just sitting there..."

"But for most companies developing a game, even scraping together two or three million is a struggle, and they can't keep up later on... President Tao's *Reign of Sovereignty* is an exception. For games with an investment of less than 5 million, the success rate is less than 10%. But for games with an investment of over 20 million, not a single one has failed..."

Shi Yuzhu spoke on stage with soaring passion, but the industry peers listening below frowned.

They even felt a sense of fear.

The sharp contrast made Tao Chenggang seem all the more endearing.

The reporters on site grew even more excited; they already knew what their headline would be: Capital and Grassroots Compete on the Same Stage, Who Will Have the Last Laugh?

The sub-forum where Chen Guiliang was located, however, had casual online games as its theme.
